title: "Please Do Not Disturb"
subtitle: Not the best time for a cleanup.

trails.title: Necessary Buys
trails.description: She's a reliable and attentive owner of the motel, always making sure her supplies are well-stocked, even those that her guests may not need ...

content.text:
August 1989

Bought:

Blue Jay coffee beans, 5 lbs (with filters)

River Valley bedsheets, 15 sets—Going through these too fast, need a countermeasure.

Second-hand TV, 1 set—A good deal, "haunted, spooky shadows within," the seller said, hah!

Sold:

Cowboy brand toolkit, 1 set

October 1989

Bought:

Thanksgiving decorations, 1 set

Pecan Grove air fresheners, 1 dozen —Bloodstain trick is too simple. Need to have a word with "it."

"Light of the South" bulbs, 1 dozen—Pretty crumby, but affordable and useful.

Fresh cream, 3 pints—From Old Stewart's ranch, yum.

Maybe get some candy next time?

November 1989

Bought:

Texas trail candy, 5 boxes—Yum.

Marigold body wash, 1 dozen—Smells too strong.

January 1990

Bought:

Seven Star tea bags, 3 boxes

Fresh ranch butter, 15 lbs

River Valley bedsheets, 12 sets—Hope this batch lasts longer.

Sold:

Second-hand TV, 1 set—Sorry, darling, but it's time to say goodbye.

items.text: Argus presses the speaker button on the telephone.
A familiar tapping sound comes from the other end of the line.

items.speaker: Telephone
items.text: *tap, tap, tap, tap*

items.speaker: Telephone
items.text: *tap*

items.speaker: Telephone
items.text: *tap, tap—tap—tap*

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: HELP.

items.speaker: Telephone
items.text: *tap, tap—*

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: BAA. Is that the sound of a sheep?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: You noticed it, too, huh?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Ain't no way that's a human on the other end. It's gotta be some kind of animal.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Animal?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Based on those sounds and the tracks in the dust, I figure it's something small like a—
She stops.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: One sec, boss.
She fishes something out of her pocket and pops it into her mouth.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Picrasma candy?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Using your arcane skill so frequently must be tiring. You should take a break.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: The job ain't done yet. Far too early to rest.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Don't worry, boss. It's just a condition that runs in my family, no biggie.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What are its side effects?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Ha, boss. You expect a merc to reveal her weakness? We ain't that close yet.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: One thing I can tell you, though, is that I suffer the side effects as long as my eyes are open. Luckily, I've got cutting-edge technology at my disposal.
She holds up the candy between her fingers.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: They're safe, efficient, and, most importantly, satisfy my sweet tooth.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: They may be called candy, but they're actually medicine and ought to be used following medical instructions. You should know that.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Gimme a break, boss. What do doctors know about my life?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: I use these candies whenever I need them. Ain't that the whole point?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But ...
Argus motions for her to be quiet.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Shh! Did you hear that?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Hear what?
Argus lowers her voice.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: A heartbeat, right outside the door. Someone's eavesdropping on us.
Thump, thump, thump.
She crouches down.
Thump, thump, thump …
With a faint clink, she loads her shotgun.
Thump, thump, thump, thump, thump …
Then she swiftly turns the door handle.
*gasp*
The eavesdropping girl nearly falls forward into the room as the door swings open.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Care to explain why you're here, Ms. Kimberly?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Just how obsessed are you with Mr. Stefen, huh? Even now, after his death?

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: Oh, n-no, it's not what you think! I was just looking for my toy, and it just so happens—

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Toy?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: You know, it ain't my style to point a gun at an unarmed person, but sometimes you gotta do what you gotta do. Especially when they're speaking with a forked tongue.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Five.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: I told you, I was just looking for something.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Four.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: Are you joking?! Why won't you believe me?!
She stomps her feet anxiously, making the floor tremble a little.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Three.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: I-I didn't ...
She closes her eyes as if she has made a decision.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Two.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: One.
She pulls the trigger.
The bullet flies past Ms. Kimberly's ear. Her face turns pale. She curls up, desperately trying to make herself smaller.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: Don't kill me. D-Don't kill me, please. I didn't do anything.
Her fingers tremble uncontrollably as black claws extend from her fingertips.
She looks at the claws in shock, quickly tucking them into her chest, then looks nervously at the two of them.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I saw the name "Kimberly" in Matilda's report.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'd thought it was just a coincidence. But now I realize it wasn't.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Ms. Kimberly, you're a member of Manus Vindictae, aren't you?

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: I swear, I didn't do anything wrong! All I did was follow my partner like the people in black told me to.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Who's your partner?

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: I'm hungry all the time, so hungry. Oh, how I envy the likes of you. You can store your food in so many ways.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: You have enough bread and water in your barns to last an entire winter, and your pastures are full of meat and dairy products. But my food ...

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: I promise, all I'm trying to do is get back what I lost.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: There's no need to be afraid. We won't hurt you, as long as you tell me the name of your partner.
Ms. Kimberly's eyes dart around.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: Um. If I tell you her name, will you let me go?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: That depends on your sincerity.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: Sh-She's called Ms. Grace.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What's your purpose here?

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: I don't know! Those people in black told me to follow Ms. Grace's orders, but she hasn't asked me to do anything since we got here.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: She must be hiding something from me, but I couldn't care less! I just want to eat!
She speaks earnestly, but her other hand pulls something out of her pocket.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: Heh heh.
She gives a sly smile and crushes the item in her hand, releasing a veil of thick black smoke.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: You annoying little brats can catch me in your dreams!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: She's casting a teleport ritual. Argus, your assistance! We can't let her get away!
*bang*
In a final burst of smoke, Ms. Kimberly vanishes.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Tsk, she disappeared fast.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: At least now we can draw some conclusions.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Manus Vindictae has set their eyes on this motel.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Under the name of the Order of Enlightenment, they used this place as a base and conducted some failed ritual experiments before they left.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Manus Vindictae. I've heard of them. That infamous group of arcanists.
She looks worried.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: If Kayla falls into their hands ...

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Things won't turn out well, will they?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I wouldn't worry too much. They usually only target pure-blooded arcanists.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Alright, that's a relief. Kayla's bloodline is a hundred percent human.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But why would Manus Vindictae choose to come here specifically?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What are they trying to do?
Entrance, Tuesday's Motel
The conversation continues under the neon lights of the motel.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: I was worried you wouldn't be able to make your way back, so I lit the porch light for you. Oh, but how annoying that these moths keep fluttering around.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Cut the crap, lady.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Where's Vertin? Take me to her.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: I rarely turn on this light. My baby never gets lost, you see.
She gives a faint smile.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: But a young, spirited child such as yourself always needs a light to lead the way. Am I right?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: To the weary traveler, this light is a shelter; to a child, it's a mother; and to you? What does this light mean to you?
The maid's face flushes red.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: No matter who they are, people need a light to shine through the darkness—to chase away their fears. Don't you agree?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Are you a member of the Order of Enlightenment?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Order of Enlightenment?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Oh, you mean those troublesome guests.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Guests?
The maid ignores her question and continues talking to herself.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: I don't like them one bit. They've scribbled all over the place and made a mess of the rooms. They hurt my baby!

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Oh, my poor baby. Shh. Don't be scared. Everything's alright now.
She gently comforts the child in her arms, patting the swaddling cloth softly.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Are they still here?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Oh, of course. They made an offer that I couldn't refuse, after all.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: How much did they pay you?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Oh, you are naive, my sweet child. There are countless things in this world that money can't buy.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: A traveler can't buy the sudden appearance of a hotel at just the right time. A crying child can't buy the comforting embrace of their mother.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Ha. And I can't buy that thrilling satisfaction brought by sweet darkness.
The maid's near-neurotic muttering is getting on Lilya's nerves.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Enough of your endless rambling!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I can't waste any more time talking to you. I can't ...
With every blink, Lilya's sight becomes increasingly blurred. She can just about make out the maid's smile.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Aha.
She gently soothes the dazed pilot.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Sleep tight. Just leave everything to the adults. Yes, what a good child you are.
She flips the sign on the door to "Do Not Disturb."
